node.label: Pierre Nora
node.date_label: Essais d’ego-histoire (editor) (1987) · Between Memory and History (translated Marc Roudebush) (1989) · Les Français d’Algérie (1961)
node.description: Historian and editor whose lieux de mémoire project examined how societies materialize relations to a disappearing past. His1989 essay distinguishes mutable social memory from critical historical reconstruction and treats archives and commemorative sites as historical problems. This is Nora’s historically situated account of modern memory, not a universal description of all societies or sole authorship of the collective volumes.

incident_edges.relationship: Nora’s lieux de mémoire distinguish lived social memory from historical reconstruction and examine their materialized sites.
incident_edges.evidence_note: Own1989 pp7–9; the opposition is his argument, not a universal analytical law.

incident_edges.relationship: Nora historicizes the national framework of French memory and its weakening, connecting historiographical practice to changing collective identifications.
incident_edges.evidence_note: Own1989 pp10–12 discussion of nation, memory and historiography; selected French case, not a general claim about national histories.

incident_edges.relationship: Nora expressly invokes Halbwachs’s account of group-specific, plural memories while distinguishing memory from historical reconstruction (1989 English translation).
incident_edges.evidence_note: Printed p. 9, first paragraph, read in Marc Roudebush’s translation, alongside pp. 7–8. Nora’s memory/history opposition and civilizational language remain his historically situated formulation; the original French and Halbwachs’s full works are not newly collated.

incident_edges.relationship: Nora’s invitation to introduce O’Connell’s collection brought Le Goff to Saint Louis’s reported words, an encounter he identifies in explaining the origin of his biographical project.
incident_edges.evidence_note: Le Goff’s own opening account credits an editorial invitation and the resulting source encounter. O’Connell compiled the texts; Nora did not write them or supply the whole biography’s method. The retrospective approximate project date is not a precisely dated commission.

incident_edges.relationship: Charle credits the merits of the Lieux de mémoire project but argues that its popularity returned historians to cultural and national frames.
incident_edges.evidence_note: Own December2007 answer,published2008,163–164, explicitly says that he participated without following the master-builder’s intended direction. The institutional bibliography identifies Pierre Nora as editor of the specific1986 and1992 Lieux volumes to which Charle contributed; the interview’s unnamed editor is identified through that metadata, not presented as an explicit spoken naming. This is a qualified objection to a project’s framing and reception, not a rejection of memory research or adjudication of every chapter. Original volumes unread.

incident_edges.relationship: Uses Nora’s lieux de mémoire to treat changing traces and appropriations of the past as objects of historical inquiry.
incident_edges.evidence_note: Own2011 discussion identifies a methodological opening across periods, reinforced in2012 and2017 conclusion. This is specific analytical use, not a resource inferred merely because Dosse wrote Nora’s biography. The complete original collective work unread. Own2012 additionally recalls Nora supplying crucial details during biographical research under an agreement to maintain distance; this bounded informant contribution is consolidated here, not a claim Nora controlled or endorsed the finished book.
